summary: Daraxonrasib (Rasonque) is a first-in-class oral RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor approved August 26, 2026 for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent chemotherapy. Approval was based on the randomized Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, which showed nearly doubled median overall survival versus standard chemotherapy. The recommended dose is 300 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Key warnings include dermatologic and soft tissue toxicity, stomatitis and oral disorders, diarrhea, gastrointestinal perforation, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, and embryo-fetal toxicity. The most common adverse reactions are rash, diarrhea, stomatitis, nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, edema, decreased appetite, and hemorrhage.

moa: Daraxonrasib is a non-covalent, active-state (RAS(ON)) tri-complex multi-RAS inhibitor. It binds cyclophilin A and active GTP-bound RAS to form a tri-complex that blocks RAS effector binding, inhibiting downstream MAPK signaling. It targets multiple RAS variants including KRAS G12D, G12V, G12R, G12C, G12A, and wild-type RAS, suppressing tumor cell proliferation and survival in RAS-driven cancers such as pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to daraxonrasib or any excipient
monitor: Skin and soft tissue for rash, ulceration, or infection
Mouth and oropharynx for stomatitis and oral disorders
Stool frequency and hydration status for diarrhea
New or worsening respiratory symptoms for interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis
Signs of gastrointestinal perforation (severe abdominal pain, fever)
relative: Prior or active interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis
History of severe dermatologic or soft tissue toxicity on prior targeted therapy
Gastrointestinal risk factors for perforation (diverticulitis, ulcers, concomitant NSAIDs or corticosteroids)

preg: Based on its mechanism of action, daraxonrasib can cause fetal harm. There are no available human data. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and after the last dose per prescribing information.
lact: There are no data on the presence of daraxonrasib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and after the final dose per prescribing information.
renal: No established dose adjustment in renal impairment. Monitor closely in moderate to severe impairment and for dehydration secondary to diarrhea or vomiting.
hepatic: No established dose adjustment; elevated transaminases have been reported. Monitor liver tests and withhold or modify therapy for severe hepatic adverse reactions per prescribing information.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive gastrointestinal and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver tests (AST, ALT, bilirubin); monitor complete blood counts and pregnancy status; evaluate respiratory symptoms with imaging if interstitial lung disease is suspected.
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; swallow tablets whole.
major: Drugs that increase gastrointestinal perforation risk (NSAIDs, systemic corticosteroids) - additive risk; monitor closely
minor: No major CYP-mediated interaction requiring dose change is established in the summary labeling; review concomitant medicines per full prescribing information.
moderate: Other agents associated with pneumonitis or severe dermatologic toxicity - additive organ toxicity; monitor

counsel: Take once daily, with or without food, at about the same time; swallow tablets whole
Report any rash, blistering, skin sores, nail changes, or mouth sores promptly
Report diarrhea early and stay hydrated; seek care for severe abdominal pain or fever
Report new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (possible lung inflammation)
Use effective contraception during treatment and do not breastfeed; tell your team about all other medicines

pearls: First-in-class RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor active across KRAS G12 variants and wild-type RAS, a target present in more than 90 percent of pancreatic cancers
RASolute 302 showed nearly doubled median overall survival versus standard chemotherapy (13.2 months versus 6.7 months) in previously treated metastatic disease
Skin, mouth, and diarrhea toxicities dominate management; early reporting and dose holds keep most patients on therapy
Permanently discontinue for gastrointestinal perforation or confirmed interstitial lung disease
Embryo-fetal toxicity: verify pregnancy status and require effective contraception
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, then resume the regular schedule. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for daraxonrasib overdose. Manage with supportive care and monitor for exaggerated toxicities including skin, gastrointestinal, and pulmonary effects. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
